title: Curio Hookable Agent Manifest (v1)
description: Schema for a Curio hookable-agent manifest.json. An agent ships in a directory named '<agentId>@<major>', the major of its version, containing this manifest and a prompts/ directory with its prompt assets, referenced by path and digest; a page of Curio's agent text, such as the preamble, is named 'curio:<path>' instead. The agents Curio ships are such directories in its agents/ folder, read by the same loader as an uploaded agent, beside the base entry (kind 'base'), which holds the pages they share. Field names are camelCase. Agent package ids begin with 'agent.', then name the publisher and the agent ('agent.curio.dataflow-builder'), as Discovery source ids begin with 'source.'. Capabilities are semantic behavior contracts, kept independent of the prompt files that implement them. This schema is the canonical spec; the backend validator in utk_curio/backend/app/agents/domain/manifest.py implements the supported subset. User-facing overview: docs/AGENT-CATALOG.md.

$schema.description: Pointer to this schema. Conventionally a relative path or the raw GitHub URL of the schema file.

id.description: Agent package id: 'agent.', the publisher, then the agent's name, each a kebab-case segment, e.g. 'agent.acme.my-helper' or 'agent.curio.dataflow-builder'.

version.description: Semver-style version. Pre-release / build metadata accepted. The on-disk directory is '<id>@<major>', the version's major: a newer version of the same major replaces it.

name.description: Human-readable agent name shown in the Agent Catalog.

kind.description: 'agent' for an agent, or 'base' for the base entry, the folder in Curio's agents/ that holds the pages every agent Curio ships reads (agents/agent.curio.builtin@1), as packages/curio.builtin@1 is the base of the nodes. A base entry lists its 'pages' and is no agent: no catalog lists it, no agent delegates to it, and an upload of one is refused.

pages.description: A base entry's pages, each a .md file by its path in its folder, such as 'default_preamble.md' or 'rules/plan-rules.md'. Any agent names one as 'curio:<path>'. The backend renders each when it starts.

category.description: Catalog category chip. Drives the drawer category filter and the hook target family.

purpose.description: One-line description shown in catalog cards.

listed.description: true for a catalog card; false for a helper, which runs only as other agents' delegate and is never listed, installed or attached.

order.description: The agent's place in the roster: the agent details window names the agents that ask for a mode in this order. No two agents Curio ships share one.

catalog.description: Where an agent Curio ships stands in the Agent Catalog. Read only for the agents in Curio's agents/ folder, each of which must give it; an upload that sets it is refused.

workedExamples.description: Whether a run of the agent under its instruction, or a prompt run in its place, is given worked examples: the shipped dataflows closest to its task, in its runtime slot. A mode says so for itself (capabilities[].workedExamples). Read for the agents Curio ships.

skills.description: The skills the agent's runs may hold, by name: a skill Curio ships (a folder of its skills/) or one the account holds of its own. Its chat lists them, beyond those its preamble holds, and loads one with skill.read when a task needs it; a run with no tools is handed the ones its task needs. Without this field, every skill Curio ships; an empty list, none.

capabilities.description: Semantic capability contracts this agent declares. Capabilities are discovered/resolved/substituted by id; they never grant authorization and are independent of prompt files.

id.description: Semantic capability id: two or more dot-separated lowercase segments, e.g. 'node.explain', 'dataflow.orchestrate', 'package.recommend'. Must NOT contain a prompt filename, path separator, underscore, '.txt' or '.md' — capability ids are behavior contracts, not asset paths.

instruction.description: The prompts key of this capability's own instruction, which makes the capability a mode. A delegated run of the capability runs this prompt in place of 'instruction'; an attached run always runs 'instruction'. Must name an entry in prompts.

reads.description: Context a run of this capability reads.

requiredConfig.description: Catalog settings a run of this capability receives, by key, for example 'keywordTypes'. Their values are the user's, edited in the Agent Catalog, and reach the run as data after its instruction. A key Curio does not define is skipped.

label.description: What the capability does, in the plain words the agent details window lists it by, as a mode other agents, Solve or the agent itself ask for. Capabilities with one label are one mode. Read for the agents Curio ships, where a capability without a label is no mode; any other agent's capability is listed by its id.

workedExamples.description: Whether a run of this mode is given worked examples. Only a mode, a capability with an 'instruction', takes it; any other run follows the agent's workedExamples. Read for the agents Curio ships.

skills.description: The skills every run of this capability is handed, by name: its own procedures, whatever the agent's skills are.

oneOf.description: An agent id: every capability of that agent may be delegated.
An agent id and the only capabilities of that agent that may be delegated.

delegatesTo.description: Agents this agent may delegate to, in preference order, each named once. Expresses a preferred/required implementation only; it grants nothing and never auto-imports or auto-installs. An entry may name this agent itself only in the object form, and only with capabilities that are its own modes (capabilities with an 'instruction'): the agent then hands that work to its own mode.

requiresAgents.description: Hard dependencies: agents that must be installed alongside this one. Every entry MUST also appear in delegatesTo, must not be this agent's own id, and must not repeat. Install resolves the closure and remove refuses while a dependent is still installed.

prompts.description: Prompt assets referenced by package-relative path and SHA-256 digest. Prompt filenames are implementation assets, never capability ids.

path.description: Path to the prompt file inside the package, relative to its root. Must be contained inside the package: no leading '/', no '..' segment, and no leading '-'. Or 'curio:<path>', a page of Curio's agent text by its path in the base entry, such as 'curio:default_preamble.md', the preamble Curio shares with every agent: it is read from Curio, rendered, an upload carries no file for it, and an export carries it as 'prompts/<path>'. A 'curio:' path that leads out of the base entry, or names no page it lists, is refused.

runs.description: When this prompt runs, in the words the agent details window shows, for a prompt that is neither 'system', 'instruction' nor a mode's instruction, such as the Node Builder's 'autk-grammar'. Read for the agents Curio ships.

skills.description: The skills every run of this prompt is handed, by name: the procedures it follows, whatever the agent's skills are. Only 'instruction' names them, and they reach its chat from its first message and each capability with no instruction of its own; a mode's own are its capability's skills.

sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the asset bytes.

contracts.description: Package-relative paths to the input/output JSON Schemas for this agent's capability contract. RESERVED: accepted for forward compatibility but not read by the current manifest parser, so it has no effect on how an agent runs.

compatibleTargets.description: Where this agent can attach. Drives which nodes/canvas glow and which palette drag targets accept it.

requires.description: For a node target, what the node may be, any one of them enough: a flag its template declares (e.g. 'loadsDataset') or a template id it has (e.g. 'data-loading'). Empty means any node.

inputs.description: Context this agent reads and the catalog settings every run of it receives.

requiredConfig.description: Catalog settings every run of this agent receives, by key. See capabilities[].requiredConfig for settings only one capability reads.

configuration.description: Non-secret configuration options and defaults. RESERVED: accepted for forward compatibility but not read by the current manifest parser, so it has no effect on how an agent runs. The values a run does receive are catalog settings, declared with inputs.requiredConfig and capabilities[].requiredConfig.

providerRequirements.description: Provider capability requirements (e.g. 'structured-output', 'code-generation'), a preference: an agent runs on the LLM configuration its user chose for it in API Settings, outside the manifest. Credentials and configurations never belong here.

tools.description: Typed, allowlisted tool requirements — not executable code or permission grants.

id.description: Tool id: two or more dot-separated lowercase segments, e.g. 'web.search', 'node.content.write'. Same grammar as a capability id, and enforced the same way at import: a bare name like 'web' is rejected.

settingsDefaults.description: Immutable, non-secret seed suggestions and a reviewed profile-family id/version. Not active policy; a manifest cannot create a new trusted profile family implicitly.

provenance.description: Origin and trust of the definition.
